html:
The Battle of Dandanaqan was fought in May 1040 near Merv, in Turkmenistan, where the Seljuk Turks under Tughril and Chaghri crushed the army of the Ghaznavid sultan Masud.

The Seljuks were Oghuz Turkic herders, ancestors of the Turkmen, who had crossed into Khorasan. Masud's heavy army, with war elephants, marched for days through the desert without water, and was beaten in three days of fighting at a small fort.

The victory gave the Seljuks Khorasan and opened Iran to them. Within twenty years Tughril entered Baghdad, and the Seljuk Empire went on to rule from Central Asia to Anatolia, where its heirs fought at Manzikert. The Turkmen still see the Seljuks as one of their founding dynasties.
